content.summary: The degree-sum constraints withstand the assigned check. Both frozen hashes match. I found a concrete counterexample to dropping selected-point distinctness from the pair cap, but the manuscript and formal application retain that hypothesis.

checks.scope: Four-star degree sum and prerequisite pair caps
checks.method: Evaluated both per-member inequalities for j=0,...,4; inspected FourStar and SupportFacts; enumerated all triples of an eight-member adversarial family.
checks.observation: Binomial values 0,0,1,3,6 dominate 2j-3 and j-1. Summation gives 2D<=84+S<=120, hence D<=60. Two- and three-star union bounds give 34 and 46 using respectively one and three pair caps. Eight binary transversals of three disjoint pairs, each augmented by one common point, are sunflower-free; repeating that point makes the supposed pair-codegree eight. The formal cap explicitly requires unequal points, and four_degree_sum_le_sixty supplies all six inequalities, preventing this misuse.
